verification_report.summary: The proof is correct and complete. The binomial expansion validly yields p(x+y)=p(x)+yp'(x)+y^2S(x,y), and substitution of y=p(x)-x together with cancellation in R[x] proves that p(x)-x divides 1+p'(x). The degree argument excludes all degrees at least two, the resulting affine divisibility condition forces slope 1 or -1, and the explicitly chosen polynomials q verify every claimed case, including p(x)=x. The statement is self-contained, and the proof contains no external citations, internal fact-id dependencies, or hard-prohibition violations.
